text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired for rotation 'network-team' — reason: ALB target group health failing (TLS handshake) in us-west-2. Auto-escalation to oncall rotation.

pagerduty: Incident created: PD-INC-10987. Initial urgency: high. Pages sent to rotation: network-team -> alex_sre. Escalation policy: 5m -> infra -> lead.

alex_sre: ack — taking this, marking as P1. Starting triage (lb, certs, recent deploys).

mira_net: i'm on call too, joining. pulling target health now.

mira_net: (run) ```aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-api/abcd1234 --region us-west-2```
Output snippet:
```
TargetHealthDescriptions: [
  { Target: {Id: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6}, HealthCheckPort: "443", TargetHealth: {State: "unhealthy", Reason: "TLS handshake error"} },
  { Target: {Id: i-0f1e2d3c4b5a6}, HealthCheckPort: "443", TargetHealth: {State: "unhealthy", Reason: "TLS handshake error"} }
]
```

alex_sre: ok — two targets failing TLS handshakes. pulling recent changes. anyone touched ALB listener certs or security policy?

sam_infra: i ran a rolling ALB listener policy update ~10m ago to enforce TLS1.2 minimum and an updated ciphersuite (PR #847). applied via terraform: `terraform apply -auto-approve` (hash: c3f1ab2).

alex_sre: that aligns with timing. hypothesis: policy change is causing backend handshake mismatch (client vs server). mira, can you check instance certs + nginx TLS config?

mira_net: checking nginx on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6:
```
ssh ec2-user@i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6 'sudo openssl s_client -connect localhost:443 -servername api.redwood.dev'
CONNECTED(00000003)
139728...:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:334
```

mira_net: instance stack returning strange version errors — looks like nginx not negotiating with new ciphers. config shows `ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_ciphers` uses some legacy ordering.

alex_sre: decision: rollback the ALB listener policy to previous cipher set and re-evaluate. sam, can you roll back the listener change? If rollback not possible quickly, we'll fail traffic to a healthy target group in another region as fallback.

sam_infra: rolling back now. command: ```terraform workspace select prod && terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars -target=aws_lb_listener.lb_listener --auto-approve```
Planning: will replace listener policy to previous (hash b7a9f). Applying...

incident-bot: Canary failover enabled: shifting 40% of traffic to tg-api-secondary (us-east-1) via routing policy to reduce customer impact.

lia_support: received first customer report: "TLS cert mismatch" on api.redwood.dev for 8 customers across two accounts. Listing top three: AcmeCorp, DataRain, ZapHub. They've opened support tickets.

jordan_pm: how bad is the customer impact? will this cause degraded API calls for all customers in us-west-2?

alex_sre: impact: intermittent 502/SSL handshake errors for requests routed to affected targets in us-west-2. Some retries succeed due to routing to healthy backends or us-east fallback. We should update status page and notify top customers.

mira_net: rollback finished on ALB listener — terraform reported success. re-checking target health...

mira_net: (run) ```aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-api/abcd1234 --region us-west-2```
Output snippet:
```
TargetHealthDescriptions: [
  { Target: {Id: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6}, TargetHealth: {State: "healthy"} },
  { Target: {Id: i-0f1e2d3c4b5a6}, TargetHealth: {State: "healthy"} }
]
```

alex_sre: nice — targets healthy again. removing canary failover and rebalancing back to primary routing.

incident-bot: Routing policy updated: removed canary — 100% traffic -> tg-api (us-west-2).

mira_net: quick note: DNS TTL is 300s but we didn't change DNS records. issue was purely listener/cipher mismatch. some CDN edges cached TLS-negotiation results which explains cert mismatch reports. clearing CDN cache for api.redwood.dev now.

lia_support: update sent to affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem. preparing status page blurb.

jordan_pm: good. can we get a short RCA + next steps for follow-up? we'll need comms ready for customers impacted.

alex_sre: immediate follow-ups: 1) add a test matrix for listener policy changes on staging with same cipher suites, 2) add automated smoke-tests for TLS handshake post-listener-change, 3) add circuit-breaker to shift traffic faster during similar failures.

sam_infra: i'll add a terraform guardrail to require a canary window and automated smoke test pass before promoting listener policy to prod. PR coming.

pagerduty: Incident PD-INC-10987 acknowledged by alex_sre, status: mitigated, escalation(s) triggered: infra lead paged at +5m.

alex_sre: leaving the pager open for 30m monitoring. will close after stable window. thanks team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager closed by alex_sre after mitigation and validation. Post-incident tasks created: OP-415 (smoke tests), OP-416 (cipher compatibility matrix), OP-417 (status page template).

lia_support: adding customer follow-ups to OP-416 and tagging account owners.

mira_net: adding notes to runbook: if TLS handshake errors spike after listener change, rollback listener policy and enable failover; check CDN edge cache.

alex_sre: all good. moving to postmortem. leaving this thread for the notes.
